heading: PROVINCE OF CENTRAL KALIMANTAN
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gunung Mas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
7. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Community is an individual, community group, including parents and family.

10. Prevention is all efforts to eliminate all risks and adverse impacts of violence against Women and Children.
11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
12. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as FPK2PA, is a coordination forum for handling victims of Violence against Women and Children whose implementation is tiered at the regency and sub-district levels.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect the rights of children, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Protection of Women and Children is organized based on the principles of:
a. respect, fulfillment, protection, promotion, and enforcement of rights; and
b. legal certainty.

heading: Article 12

Article 12

1. The form of Child Protection services as referred to in Article 11 letter a includes:
a. legal aid;
b. social rehabilitation services; and
c. social reintegration services.
2. Further provisions regarding Child Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 13
Part Four

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. Prevention of violations of Children's rights shall be implemented by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph I]) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a work network;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Prevention based on partnership patterns with the Community, private sector, non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Child Protection.
3. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. increasing Children's productivity;
b. developing Children's self-potential;
c. preventing pregnancy at a young age;
d. reducing maternal and infant mortality rates; and
e. preventing the occurrence of domestic Violence.
4. The establishment of a work network as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, includes the Regional Government's work partners in the implementation of Prevention of rights violations in the form of family partners.
5. Further provisions regarding the Prevention of violations of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

translated_text:
Article 15

heading: Part One
translated_text:
Part One

General

heading: Article 17
Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The Regional Government in carrying out the responsibility of institutionalizing Gender mainstreaming as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (3) letter b for Women's and Children's Protection shall administer a Women's and Children's data information system.
2. The Women's data information system as referred to in paragraph (1) is an inseparable part of the Children's data information system.
3. The Women's and Children's information system as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.
4. Gender mainstreaming as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be administered in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children, the Regional Government must carry out cross-sectoral coordination with related institutions.
2. In the implementation of coordination for Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall establish a coordination team for Protection of Women and Children.
3. In the coordination forum activities as referred to in paragraph (2), the coordination team for Protection of Women and Children shall have the duties to:
a. prepare the necessary materials related to the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and
b. convey the results, obstacles, and solutions undertaken to overcome obstacles in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
4. The coordination forum as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted periodically, at least 2 (two) times in 1 (one) year.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Prevention of Violence Against Women and Children

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts for the Prevention of Violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (3) letter e and paragraph (4) letter i in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for Protection of Women and Children victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-Violence values toward Women and Children; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the empowerment of Women and Protection of Children victims of Violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for victims by involving Community elements; and
b. encouraging Community awareness of the importance of protection for victims of Violence.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Institutions

heading: Article 21
Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

P2TP2A

Article 22

1. The implementation of services for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by P2TP2A.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in the form of functional relationship patterns among components directed to achieve common goals.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. P2TP2A provides services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house.
2. In the event that P2TP2A does not yet have a safe house, then victims of Violence shall be referred to other integrated service centers that have a safe house.

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

1. P2TP2A consists of several counseling fields.
2. The counseling fields as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. law;
b. health;
c. spiritual; and
d. psychology.
3. The implementation of counseling shall be carried out by counselors and may be implemented by involving related parties.

heading: Article 25
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

Provisions regarding the implementation of services by P2TP2A as referred to in Article 22 paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

FPK2PA

Article 27

1. In order to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of Violence, FPK2PA shall be established.
2. FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. Regional FPK2PA;
b. sub-district FPK2PA; and
c. village/ward FPK2PA.
3. The establishment of Regional FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall be stipulated by the Regent.
4. The establishment of sub-district FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b shall be stipulated by the sub-district head.
5. The establishment of village/ward FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be stipulated by the village/ward head.
6. Further provisions regarding FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Part One

Obligations and Responsibilities of Parents and/or Family

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Parents have the obligation and responsibility to:
a. care for, nurture, educate, manage and protect family members;
b. develop family members in accordance with the enhancement of their abilities, talents, and interests; and
c. prevent marriage at Child age.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

The enhancement of the role and participation of the family in Protection of Women and Children shall be carried out through:
a. prevention of marriage at Child age;
b. bringing Women closer to health services; and
c. strengthening family resilience.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community Involvement

heading: Article 30
CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 31

1. The Regent is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision on the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training;
d. monitoring and evaluation; and
e. reporting.
4. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children in accordance with standard norms, procedures and criteria implemented by Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
5. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
6. In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection must report periodically to the Regent.
7. In the case of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2), Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus, the Community, agencies and/or related institutional organizations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

EVALUATION

Article 32

1. Evaluation of the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted based on documents of service implementation, empowerment, Prevention, fulfillment and monitoring results of the administration of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes evaluation of process, impact and results.
4. The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be material for Regional Apparatus to prepare reports which are subsequently submitted to the Regent.
5. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be implemented at least 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year.
6. Further provisions regarding evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

heading: REPORTING
translated_text:
REPORTING

Article 33

1. Reporting of evaluation results as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (5) shall be material for the Regent's consideration in making policies for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. Reports on the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year and at any time when necessary.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FUNDING

Article 34

Funding for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children shall be sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 35

The establishment of regional technical implementing units that administer the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in Article 21 paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the Regional financial capacity.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Gunung Mas Regency.

NUMBER 1 OF 2021 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNG MAS REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and qualified. Through the role of Women in the family, the Community and the state, strong generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, until now Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom inherent dignity and worth as a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and avoid wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as stated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.
